Let the roots of the cubic be \(r_1,r_2,r_3\), so they are \(\alpha^2,\beta^2,\gamma^2\) in some order.

For any possible value of \(\alpha+\beta+\gamma\), its negative is also possible by replacing \((\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\) with \((-\alpha,-\beta,-\gamma)\). Thus the possible values come in \(\pm\) pairs, except possibly \(0\). Since there are exactly \(7\) distinct values, one of them must be \(0\).

So there exist square roots \(a,b,c\) of \(r_1,r_2,r_3\) such that
\[
a+b+c=0.
\]
Let
\[
q=ab+bc+ca.
\]
Since \(a+b+c=0\),
\[
r_1+r_2+r_3=a^2+b^2+c^2=-2q.
\]
By Vieta’s formulas,
\[
r_1+r_2+r_3=\frac n6,
\]
so
\[
q=-\frac n{12}.
\]
Also,
\[
q^2=(ab+bc+ca)^2=a^2b^2+b^2c^2+c^2a^2+2abc(a+b+c).
\]
Because \(a+b+c=0\),
\[
q^2=r_1r_2+r_2r_3+r_3r_1.
\]
Again by Vieta,
\[
r_1r_2+r_2r_3+r_3r_1=n-11.
\]
Therefore
\[
\left(-\frac n{12}\right)^2=n-11,
\]
so
\[
n^2-144n+1584=0.
\]
Thus
\[
n=12 \quad \text{or} \quad n=132.
\]

Now check \(n=132\). The polynomial is
\[
x^3-22x^2+121x-400=(x-16)(x^2-6x+25),
\]
whose roots are
\[
16,\quad 3+4i,\quad 3-4i.
\]
Choose
\[
\alpha=-4,\quad \beta=2+i,\quad \gamma=2-i.
\]
Then
\[
\alpha^2=16,\quad \beta^2=3+4i,\quad \gamma^2=3-4i,
\]
and \(\alpha+\beta+\gamma=0\). The eight sign choices produce the values
\[
0,\ \pm 8,\ 4+2i,\ 4-2i,\ -4+2i,\ -4-2i,
\]
which are exactly \(7\) distinct values.

Therefore the greatest such integer is
\[
\boxed{132}.
\]
